description: A React UI built on the `react-vite` template + `react-component-library` adoptions presents a validation-results view (per-scenario findings table) and a search view (free-text + provenance filter).

requirements.description: A React UI application built on the `react-vite` template using `react-component-library` adoptions must provide a validation-results view. This view must display a per-scenario findings table showing scenario name, finding type, affected path, severity, and message for all Findings returned by `ui-health validate`.
requirements.title: UI Inspection Surface - Validation Results View

validation.notes: Findings table component renders a row for each Finding object in the input data
Each row displays: scenario_name, finding_type, path, severity, message columns
Empty findings state displays a success indicator
Start the UI, trigger a validate action for a scenario with known Findings, and confirm all Findings appear in the table
Confirm the UI is built using the react-vite template and adopts components from react-component-library
Confirm table supports sorting by severity and scenario name
Table renders 1000 findings without UI jank (frame rate stays above 30fps)
Developers can visually inspect the health of all scenarios from a single dashboard without running CLI commands manually

requirements.description: The React UI must provide a search view that allows free-text search across all indexed UI surfaces and supports filtering results by ComponentProvenance status (CUSTOM, ADOPTED_UNMODIFIED, ADOPTED_MODIFIED, UNKNOWN). Results must display component name, scenario, adoption status, library, library_version, and drift_hash.
requirements.title: UI Inspection Surface - Search View with Provenance Filter

validation.notes: Search input component debounces user input before triggering a query
Provenance filter component renders all four adoption status options as selectable filters
Search result card displays all required fields: component name, scenario, adoption_status, library, library_version, drift_hash
Enter a search term in the UI and confirm results appear matching the indexed corpus
Apply a provenance filter and confirm only results matching the selected adoption_status are displayed
Confirm the UI calls the `ui-health search query` API endpoint (or equivalent backend) for results
Search results are displayed within 2 seconds of user input (after debounce) for a corpus of 10,000 records
Developers can audit which components are custom vs. adopted and identify modified adoptions that may need review

title: UI inspection surface
